entities.summary: William Richard Frisell is an American jazz guitarist. He first came to prominence at ECM Records in the 1980s, as both a session player and a leader. He went on to work in a variety of contexts, notably as a participant in the Downtown Scene in New York City, where he formed a long working relationship with composer and saxophonist John Zorn. He was also a longtime member of veteran drummer Paul Motian's groups from the early 1980s until Motian's death in 2011. Since the late 1990s, Frisell's output as a bandleader has also integrated prominent elements of folk, country, rock 'n' roll, and Americana.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a key figure in the Downtown Scene and a long-time member of Paul Motian's groups, Bill Frisell played a significant role in shaping the New York City jazz scene in the 1980s and 1990s. His collaborations with John Zorn and other notable musicians helped define the sound of this era.
